title: Best Brand Style Guide Designers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a designer for a brand style guide: what it should include, how to brief it, what drives the price and the red flags.
intro: A brand style guide is the rulebook for how your brand looks and sounds: logo use, colors, fonts, images and tone. It keeps everything consistent when different people make your website, posts and packaging. Style guides often disappoint when they are pretty documents with no practical rules. This guide shows you what to ask for.

faq.q: Do I need a logo before ordering a style guide?
faq.a: Usually yes. Most style guides are built around an existing logo. Some designers offer a logo and style guide together, which suits new brands.

faq.q: What format should the style guide be in?
faq.a: A PDF is common and easy to share. Ask also for the source file, so it can be updated, and for the color codes and fonts in a form your team can copy easily.

faq.q: Does a style guide include the tone of voice?
faq.a: Some do, some cover visuals only. If you want rules for how your brand writes, such as words to use and avoid, ask for a tone-of-voice section.
The guide names the fonts, but you may need a license to use some of them, especially paid fonts on a website or in an app. Ask which fonts are free for commercial use and which need a license.

faq.q: How long should a style guide be?
faq.a: Long enough to answer the questions your team actually has, and no longer. A short guide that people use beats a long one nobody opens.
